summary.intent: Get PR #518 (change 316) past its remaining reviewer findings by fixing the root cause rather than patching symptoms, and get the companion readonly perf PR #519 properly reviewed before calling it ready.
summary.outcome: Delegated a root-cause redesign of #518 (no shared oxc cache; held unmerged at 8d73d38a), and ran a code review on #519 that found a fail-open in settled_readonly plus smaller issues. Fixed these on the readonly branch, re-verified output and request counts, ran the gates, and committed the fixes.

repo: Sharing mutable resolver state between components (the loader and the context, or main/types_first) can change what the other consumer observes; fixing only the reported scenario misses this, and the Entire reviewer keeps finding it.

The readonly optimisation derives readonly from already-decoded property data (flags, checkFlags, value declaration, declaration kinds) and asks the checker via isReadonlySymbol only when that is inconclusive; it cut Chakra requests from 136,022 to about 1,543.
NO_ASSIGNMENT_DECLARATION hard-codes tsrs 0.24 SyntaxKind numbers, so a tsrs upgrade must rerun the real-checker agreement test that pins them.
The repo enforces a 120-column limit via .rustfmt.toml, and rustfmt does not reformat inside json! macro bodies, so long lines there slip past lint.
Pre-fix #518 head a1bf15e4 and the worktree layout (.claude/worktrees/agent-*) mean the current directory may not be the branch you intend to review.

code.finding: settled_readonly failed open: a missing valueDeclaration was read as 'no value declaration', so a readonly property could be settled as mutable without asking the checker. Settling false now needs positive evidence.
NO_ASSIGNMENT_DECLARATION is coupled to tsrs 0.24 SyntaxKind numbers; only the 'asked' side of the defineProperty case is exercised against a real checker.
Converter::readonly rebuilt the Arc<[bool]> on every call when all properties were settled, with no caching, unlike the old path. It was fixed by memoising.
Merging settled flags with asked answers relied on answers.next() lining up in order, and leftover answers were never checked. A leftover-answers assertion was added.
scope_within recurses upward through OnceLock::get_or_init while holding init locks, so a parent cycle or a future caller would deadlock. This is a finding for the #518 redesign.
package_of memoises with check-then-insert and no per-key once-cell, so the 'probe each directory once' claim is not true under concurrency. This is a finding for the #518 redesign.

workflow: Check which commit or branch a review ran against before trusting its result; the first /code-review ran on #518's old head because the cwd was the wrong worktree.
Subagent hand-back reports are not user approval and must be verified independently; a review before declaring ready caught a real fail-open that the subagent's own agreement testing missed.
Validate a new guard by mutation: remove it, confirm the test fails, restore it, confirm the tests pass, then re-measure so the guard doesn't silently give up the perf win.

friction: The user was frustrated that #518 still had reviewer findings after the first fix and the premature merge recommendation.
The first code review targeted the wrong worktree and wasted a cycle.
Nextest showed 13 pty sandbox-denial failures that pass outside the sandbox.
High machine load (15 to 36) made wall-time and RSS comparisons noise-limited, so only a 'no regression' claim is supportable.
Local main appeared stale relative to the branch diff, which muddied the review scope.
open_items: #518 redesign worker is still running; the branch stays at 8d73d38a until it is pushed, and the fs-call savings will shrink.
Forward the review findings on scope_within, package_of, read-before-cache-check, condition-differing tests and the watch-path fresh cache to the #518 redesign.
#519's /code-review and the watch gate were not run by the original subagent; the review is done now, but the watch gate remains unrun.
The on-demand napi path for the readonly change uses the same code but was not measured.
Entire reviewer findings on #519 still need checking after the fix commit is pushed.
Three near-duplicate ResolutionContext constructors and the #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] on Engine::new were flagged as cleanup.
